column1: # Every feature suggestion and hypothesis this project has put through the
# bar, and what happened to it. Typed by hand like the patch log is; read
# by scripts/board.py for the README and scripts/webapp.py for the app, so
# one edit here updates both surfaces and they cannot disagree.
# The status is a verdict, not a mood:
#   green    verified and helping — cleared two separate time windows and
#            is live in the engine today
#   orange   unfinished — measured but not concluded, or shipped on
#            PROBATION and still waiting on live results to confirm it
#   red      declined — tested and rejected, with the number that killed
#            it. These are kept deliberately: a dead idea that stays
#            written down does not get re-proposed every fortnight.
# Columns: status, date, area, hypothesis, verdict.

column4: Should every spelling of a club be folded onto one name, store-wide and ungated? (the bettor's call after the era-split merge surfaced the same defect at a hundred times the scale: "those names need to match smoothly. no more mistakes")
column5: Shipped, and the honest verdict is that it is a CORRECTNESS fix rather than an accuracy one. The defect is real and was measured first: the results provider changed convention on 2024-08-10, terse trading names to full legal ones, and the store kept both, so 22.2% of every row stored since then was invisible to the spelling a hand-typed fixture resolves to — 64% in ESP-L2, 61% POR-PL, 47% ENG-PL — and Chelsea, Ajax, Porto, Roma, Juventus and Valencia each lost their entire modern record. Two layers now fold it in store.load_results: the canonical key (names.canonical, the resolver's own reduction, moved to app/data/names.py so one definition serves both instead of two copies drifting) for decoration, and 276 TYPED pairs for the case no algorithm should attempt, where one spelling abbreviates a word the other spells out — Man United against Manchester United, PSV against PSV Eindhoven, Inter against FC Internazionale Milano. 552 folds, 3 refusals. THE GUARD is a fact about football rather than a similarity threshold: a club plays at most one match a day, so two spellings sharing a date are different clubs and the fold is refused however well the names match, tested against everything already in a group so three names cannot join two clubs indirectly. All three refusals are correct (Paraguay's Club Nacional against Uruguay's, Finland's FC Inter against Inter Milan, a duplicated Hapoel row). NOW THE MEASUREMENT, which does not support an accuracy claim. Replaying 12,786 fixtures since 2024-08-10 twice, fold on and off, everything else identical: abstentions fall 496 to 317, so 179 fixtures are recovered and they grade 83.80%, right at the base rate. But on the 12,290 cards that print BOTH ways tip 1 goes 83.91% to 83.88% — nothing — and on the 263 where the fold CHANGES the rung it grades 83.65% against 82.13%, which is four cards out of 263 against a standard error of 2.32 points. Where the rung is unchanged the claim moves 0.06 points on average. So the replay says: neutral. WHY the replay cannot see the live defect, which matters more than the number: a replay looks each fixture up by its OWN stored row name, so a 2025 Chelsea match is read as `Chelsea FC` and gets the correct recent rows either way — by 2025 the long name already holds more than ROLLING_MATCHES=10. The live board is different: it types `Chelsea` by hand, which resolved to the 912-row spelling whose last match was May 2024. That is priced by the staleness study registered above (a window reaching four years back costs 1.47 points within-league) and by the board itself, where clubs read on stale rows fall from 114 to 12 and the twelve that remain are genuine — clubs that left the division. 13 pending cards re-priced, four changing market outright, all in ENG-CH. THREE FAILURES found while building it, each worse than the split it repaired: folding onto the name with most rows picks the DEAD spelling (Atlético de Madrid onto Ath Madrid, whose 456 rows all predate the change, so a board typing `Atlético Madrid` resolved to nothing — the primary is now the name the league most recently played under); typed pairs keyed by variant do not COMPOSE, so FRA-L1 stating both Brest = Stade Brestois and Stade Brestois = Stade Brestois 29 silently dropped Brest from its own club; and the fold can SHRINK what resolves, since `PSG` reached `Paris SG` through an alias whose membership guard then failed. Each is now a comment beside the code that fixes it. Green because the data defect is unambiguous and the recovered fixtures are free, NOT because the engine got more accurate — it did not, and claiming otherwise on four cards would be exactly the single-window reasoning this project has rejected six times

column4: Should a club whose history is split across two names by an ERA gap be merged, when the merge file had deliberately left it split? (FC Thun and FC Vaduz: both relegated and returned, so their deep history is filed under one name and their 2026 rows under another, leaving 3 rows against a 5-match gate and two abstentions on the 2 Sep slate)
column5: Merged, after measuring the objection instead of accepting it. The file's own note said folding them would build a tip on six-year-old form — true, and now sized: across 68,341 replayed cards bucketed by how far back the rolling ten reaches, tip 1 grades 83.56% on a normal window (0-120 days), 82.17% at 730-1,460 days and 81.10% beyond four years. Raw that is -2.46 points, but the deep windows cluster in the cups and the Scottish lower divisions, which grade badly anyway; controlled WITHIN each league the drag is -1.47 points on an equal-league average over 35 leagues (-2.20 weighted, negative in 23 of 35). Real, one-directional and small — and the alternative is not a fresher tip but NO tip. The gate makes it temporary too: store._apply_merges only folds while the primary is under 5 rows, so the old form bridges the first weeks of a season and is then never read again. Checked first that no better source existed — SUI-CL holds two rows in total, both from a 2021 playoff, so the Swiss second tier simply is not stored. WHERE IT IS, a merge is the WRONG tool and must not be used: _apply_merges runs inside load_results, so a merged club clears min_matches and the cross-division fallback never fires — merging Coventry's 2000-01 Premier League rows onto its 2026 promotion would suppress a fallback that reads last season. Result on the board: both fixtures now price, SUI-SL's slice table was rebuilt (the league record gained 6 cards, FC Thun 84/100 became Thun 87/103), and Luzern v Vaduz came out orange at +5.63, STRONG, U4.5 at 1.41 against a 1.27 bar — the widest margin on the slate. Thun v Lausanne prices and correctly declines at O1.0 1.01. --reprice grew a --revive flag for this: an abstention is still an answer by default, but a pending abstention caused by a DATA defect since fixed was an answer to a different question

column4: How widespread is the split-name defect the merge file patches club by club? (asked because the scan for era splits was run store-wide rather than on the two clubs that surfaced)
column5: Far wider than the merge file can reach, and it is a RECENCY defect wearing a naming costume. The results provider changed convention on 2024-08-10 — short trading names became full legal ones — and the store kept both, so most clubs in the major leagues now hold two or three spellings: Chelsea 912 rows to 2024-05-19 alongside Chelsea FC 76 rows covering the last two seasons; Man United under Man United, Manchester United AND Manchester United FC. Grouping every name in every league by a normalised key and asking the REAL resolver which spelling a hand-typed fixture lands on, 8,329 of the 37,556 rows stored since Aug 2024 — 22.2% — are invisible to the name that wins. ESP-L2 64.2%, POR-PL 60.7%, ENG-PL 47.4%, ESP-LL 44.7%, ENG-CH 31.3%. Ajax, Porto, Roma, Juventus, Valencia, Getafe and Chelsea each lose 70-77 recent rows, i.e. their entire modern record. This is NOT what team_merges fixes: that gate fires only when the primary is under 5 rows, and Chelsea has 912, so the merge mechanism is structurally unable to see it. It is also not currently costing the board much — 1 of 37 pending cards reads stale rows (Yokohama FM, resolved onto Yokohama FC, the exact failure the aliases file header warns about) — because ingest_board keeps feeding SHORT names back in, which keeps the short spelling roughly current for any club that has already appeared. Chelsea has not, so the first Chelsea card will price on spring-2024 form. NOT FIXED, deliberately: unconditional canonicalisation rewrites club history in 27 leagues and therefore every number measured on them, which is a call for the bettor rather than a tidy-up. The staleness measurement above prices the damage at roughly 1.5 points of hit rate per affected card

column4: Should a printed rung be struck at Rule 6's SAFER NEIGHBOUR or at the rung itself? (the bettor struck U3.5 where the card printed U3.0 and noticed Unibet pays 1.45 on U3.0 against 1.29 on U3.5 — the push line pays much more and returns the stake at three goals)
column5: Safer neighbour, and for a reason worth keeping. First, the ROI tables were never confused: every script used lane=bought(mk) for BOTH the price and the settlement, which is correct because p_win('U3.0') equals p_win('U3.5') under the push-counts-as-hit convention while settle_fraction knows the difference (three goals pays 0.0 on U3.0, +1.0 on U3.5) — the hit-rate function priced and the money function settled. Then the comparison, both lines from the same fitted mu with the same margin and both settled on real results over 951 qualifying bets: bought line 1.35 odds, 75.0% win, ROI +0.86%; printed rung 1.49 odds, 57.0% win, 18.0% push, ROI +0.24%. The push line pays 10.5% more and returns less. By family U3.0->U3.5 gives +2.86% against +2.32% and U4.25->U4.5 gives -4.53% against -5.34%; applying the bar to the rung's own longer price is worse again at -1.53% on 1,967 bets, since the longer quote clears more often and admits weaker cards. THE MECHANISM: two forces oppose. The margin only bites the stake at risk, worth about P(push) x (1 - 1/overround) or roughly +0.95% for the push line; but a push returns stake at exactly 1.00 so the EDGE earns nothing on that portion, and with 18% pushing, 18% of the money sits out. With no edge the push line wins; with an edge you want more stake at risk, and the second force is larger by about 0.6 points. So the convention is right BECAUSE the rule has an edge — if the edge ever vanishes the better buy flips to the push line, which makes it a usable canary. Caveat per card: this is at derived prices, and Unibet's live board showed a 12.4% premium on U3.0 where the model implies 10.4%, so a book overpricing the push line by more than fair could favour it on that fixture — a line-shopping call, not a rule change

column4: Should measurement be restricted to the modern era? (the bettor's call: 2022-2026 is the game being played now, and a result that needs 2016 to hold is not a result about it)
column5: Adopted, and it costs almost nothing — which is the informative part. Recomputing every registered label rate on 2022-2026 only moves the required prices by at most 0.007: super green 89.72% -> 89.75% (bar 1.181 unchanged), green 87.37 -> 87.68 (1.213 -> 1.209), orange 83.42 -> 83.35 (1.271 -> 1.272), red 77.88 -> 77.73 (1.361 -> 1.364), super red 77.38 -> 77.78 (1.370 -> 1.363). The tier ordering the five labels depend on holds in both cuts. The registered rates therefore STAY: they survive the restriction inside noise, and re-freezing thresholds to chase a third decimal would break the property that makes the forward log gradeable, namely that a card scored today faces the same bar as one scored last month. It also corrects how the two-window split was described: 55,544 of the bank's 62,528 cards are ALREADY 2022 or later and only 11% predates it, so calling the full-bank split 'nine years against two' was true of the date range and misleading about the data — card density rose sharply as leagues were added, so the older half running 2015 to May 2024 is itself about 78% post-2022. The split has effectively been 2022-2024 against 2024-2026 throughout, which is a healthier test than the labels implied. The priced ROI tables were never affected: they run 2024-07 to 2026-05, two consecutive seasons

column4: Where does the decline rule's edge actually come from — the margin, or the price panel it is settled at? (asked while testing whether a looser bar could add playable lanes)
column5: The panel, and it is not close. Every figure in the odds work is settled at the MAXIMUM across football-data's ~10 books; re-settling the IDENTICAL rule at Bet365 alone takes +1.71% to +0.62%, and at the market average to -0.69%. Same shape at every bar: +8% gives +2.08 / +1.15 / -0.31 and +4% gives +0.66 / -0.47 / -1.51. About 1.1 points of ROI separates best-of-market from one book at the same bar — more than the margin choice and more than the per-league question tested the same day — and at the market average the rule loses money at EVERY bar. Line shopping is not a refinement, it is most of the edge. Practical consequence for a bettor holding Dutch accounts only: four books is a real panel but the +1.71% is against ten including Pinnacle, unreachable from NL, so the honest expectation sits between the columns. From one live board, Unibet showed 1.08 where Pinnacle paid 1.12 and 1.44 where GTbets paid 1.49. Recorded alongside: the margin sweep in UNITS WON rather than ROI shows a plateau from +5% to +10% (units +14 to +22, both windows positive) collapsing below +4% (-9.6 units at +0%), so loosening the bar to buy volume trades a working rule for negative-expectation bets; and letting RED cards back in adds nothing, +9.4 units against +17.3 without, with red alone at -6.60% on 119 bets

column4: Should the guard's price bar be per-league rather than pooled? (the engine is per-league almost everywhere — own goal mean, tempo, floor, shrink, and a consensus cap for seven leagues — while the decision layer judges all 56 competitions against one label rate and one 6% margin, and Serie A's final pick grades a point above pooled)
column5: No evidence it helps, and the reason is more useful than the result. Two variants, both shrinking the league's own record toward the pooled rate rather than replacing it — CELL (league x label) and OFFSET (league deviation applied to every label) — every rate learned on the train half and applied to the test half. MATCHED to the same 1,008 bets so it is not the volume effect: pooled +1.71%, cell prior 100 +0.64%, cell 400 +0.65%, offset 200 +0.07%. At prior 400 the two rules share 88% of their bets and of the 119 they disagree on, the ones per-league ADDS return -1.78% while the ones it DROPS return +7.17%. The mechanism: a per-league bar lowers the requirement where a league historically hits well (Serie A 1.273 -> 1.225), but a league that hits well is one the MARKET also knows hits well and whose prices are already short — so the adjustment admits short-priced bets in efficient markets and excludes the long-priced ones carrying the value. The bar works BECAUSE it is uniform and the market is not: it judges the price against a fixed reference, and market disagreement is the whole signal, so moving the reference toward the league's own record cancels what is being measured. CAVEAT that stops this being a clean rejection: pooled's advantage is one window — older +0.62 against cell-400's +0.79, where per-league is BETTER, and newer +2.80 against +0.52 — which is the single-window pattern that has killed six hypotheses here and gets no exemption. Pooled stays because it is simpler and already shipped, not because it won. Separately worth recording: per-league fairness already lives in the ENGINE, where it belongs — Serie A carries its own goal mean, tempo_factor 0.40 against the 0.50 default, a floor raised to 0.78, a relative-overreach debit against its own base rate, and the consensus cap, and the confluence score reads its own baseline and its own side split (1,295 of 1,483 cards are unders at 87.6% against overs at 76.7%)

column4: When the starred lane is struck on PRICE, should the card fall back to the other main lane if that one clears its own bar? (the bettor's rule from the Swansea card — tip 1 declined at 1.12 against a needed 1.27, so the DNB at 1.49 is next in line. NOT the score-conditional pivot already rejected: this one fires only on price, and price-conditional selection is the only thing here that has ever paid)
column5: No, and it fails in the most informative way available. On 8,121 priced cards with 2,476 carrying a priced fallback, the star bar at +6% alone returns +1.71% on 1,008 bets; adding the fallback at any margin drags the book to -0.49% or worse, and the fallback bets ALONE return -3.53% on 733 at a 41.5% hit rate against an average CLAIM of 72.2% — a thirty-point overclaim. Loosening the fallback bar HELPS (-3.53% at +0% against -6.35% at +12%), which is the tell. Sliced by how far the price sits above what the claim demands, the claim stays flat near 72% while reality collapses monotonically: +0-5% over break-even hits 52.7% (+1.03%), +5-15% hits 44.1% (+0.09%), +15-35% hits 37.2% (-5.01%), +35%+ hits 25.7% (-16.60%). Both windows agree (-3.82% older, -3.24% newer). THE LESSON, which is worth more than the rejection: a bar of the form 'price >= 1/rate x margin' selects cards where the market disagrees with `rate` most. If rate is a VALIDATED hit rate that finds market error (+1.71%); if rate is the engine's own printed claim it finds ENGINE error (-3.53%), and the harder the bar the more of it you buy. Same arithmetic, opposite sign, and the only difference is whether the denominator was ever measured. This is the sixth confirmation of the anti-predictive property and the purest one. It is why the card marks non-starred lanes claim-based. Also corrected here: the +0.83% previously quoted for the star bar included red-labelled cards, which the card already refuses — excluding them as it actually does gives +1.71%, so the shipped rule was being understated

column4: Is the SYNTHETIC draw-no-bet price behind the +6.05% actually reachable? (it was built from the best home and best away quote across all books, assuming both takeable at once and carrying no DNB-market margin — if a real quote is 6% worse the edge is gone)
column5: PASSES, at about +3.7%. Needs no history and no settlement, only today's board: fetch draw_no_bet and h2h for the same upcoming fixture in one request and compare. 60 credits, 24 fixtures, 48 comparable prices. Every single real quote is worse than the synthetic — no book gives the arbitrage away — but the shading is NOT flat with price: books shade hardest on longshots (2.60+ band, mean -6.07%, worst -16.30%) and barely at all on short favourites (1.00-1.25 band, mean -1.81%, worst -2.38%). The gated DNBs average 1.160, at the tight end. In the band actually bet (1.00-1.45) the mean gap is -2.50% and the median -2.34%, which takes the measured +6.04% to +3.66% / +3.81% rather than killing it. Break-even sits at P=1.086, a gap of -6.3%, and NONE of the 15 short-price quotes were worse than that. Two constraints the probe also found: draw-no-bet is quoted by only 1 to 4 books per fixture against 7 to 13 for the match odds, which caps stake rather than price; and NED-ED and POR-PL carry no DNB market at all, 6 of 30 fixtures probed, so a gated DNB there cannot be played as one. Residual uncertainty stated rather than hidden: the backtest's synthetic came from football-data MAX CLOSING while this probe's came from odds-api EU books pre-match, so if the former runs higher the true haircut is larger than -2.50% and this estimate is optimistic by that difference. The headroom absorbs a fair amount of it, but the number to trust is the forward log — n is 48 prices on one day against a 212-bet base result

column4: Can the guard decline on the PRICE rather than on the card? (the bettor's question: pick = tip X, but odds not worthy, so DECLINE — each label carries a measured hit rate, so it implies a break-even of 1/hit)
column5: The first positive return in the whole odds line of work, and it is mostly one lane. Bars learned on the OLDER half and applied to the newer, which is cleanly out-of-sample by accident of coverage — football-data holds two seasons against the bank's four, so all 8,121 priced cards sit in the newer half and none touched the bars judging them. The gradient runs monotonically from -1.67% playing everything to -0.21% at break-even+4%, +0.83% at +6%, +1.49% at +8% and +1.59% at +12%, crossing zero around +5% — while the HIT RATE falls the whole way, 81.8% to 69.8%. That is the point: every earlier rule selected for hit rate and watched the quote shorten by exactly as much, whereas this one selects for cards the market has not shortened ENOUGH, and it is the first rule here hunting a book error rather than an engine strength. No single cell is significant (+/-1.77 on +0.83); the gradient across seven thresholds is the evidence. Two controls survived. The label beats a plain price bar at matched selectivity by 1.2-1.3 points at the tighter bars (+0.83 vs -0.41 at +6%, +1.49 vs +0.18 at +8%), and nothing at +4%. And it is NOT a fitted-mu artifact: selecting on a derived price while settling at the same derived price would bias returns upward where extrapolation is worst, but the effect is +1.48% in the moderate band (0.6-1.1 from the 2.5 line) and -4.53% in the heavy one (1.6+), the opposite signature. HOWEVER the ladder alone only reaches break-even: -1.88% playing everything to +0.03% at +6% and +0.69% at +8%, inside its error bars. The DNB lane carries it — 212 bets at +6.05% +/-1.98 with NO price bar, rising to +15.92% on the 57 kept at +6%, on prices that are exact rather than fitted (arithmetic from the book's 1X2, no Poisson step) and splitting +6.14% older against +5.96% newer. The market implies 86.2% of decisive there and Athena wins 92.0%, which is the same underclaim found on 30 Aug now showing up as money. 65 of the 90 kept super-green cards are these DNBs. Orange for one reason: the DNB price is SYNTHESISED from the best home and best away quote across all books, which assumes both are takeable at once and carries no DNB-market margin of its own, so a real single-book draw-no-bet quote will be worse. Settling that against real quoted draw_no_bet prices now outranks the team-total probe — tip 2's signal is larger in hit-rate terms but has never shown a positive return at any price, and this just did

column4: Can a card be scored by running it back through the board's OWN searches — the league's record on that lane, then filtered to each club, to the tip's side, and to club-and-side — counting each slice above or below the league baseline as a flag for or against, then pivoting or declining when the sum is bad? (the bettor's rule, worked by hand on Aston Villa v Arsenal 31 Aug, which printed O1.5 82.0% and finished 0-1)
column5: Real, and almost entirely a restatement of the claim the card already prints. scripts/confluence.py builds every slice STRICTLY AS-OF in one forward pass — the search bar looks backwards over completed matches, so a slice it shows today contains the fixture you would have bet on, and scored that way the rule cannot fail. Over 25,494 graded cards in 57 leagues the continuous score is monotone across all ten deciles (80.62% at the bottom to 87.39% at the top) and keeping the top 40% grades 86.06% against an 83.65% base, older 86.04 newer 86.07. The hand-worked example reproduces exactly: score -2, matching the bettor's own count, with every slice within a few points of their board reading. But the ablation kills the novel part: the claim-vs-baseline check ALONE lifts +3.81 while all six searches together lift only +1.98, clubs-only lifts +0.18, and adding the club slices HALVES the claim signal. Head-to-head at matched selectivity the printed claim beats the score at every cut (+3.79 vs +2.40 keeping the top 40%), and where they disagree the claim is right — score-keeps-claim-drops grades 83.20% (below base) against claim-keeps-score-drops at 86.17%. Held fixed inside claim deciles the residual is +1.34 points, +2.14 older and +0.90 newer. Three further no's: inside the guard's RED tier the score INVERTS (79.4% at <=-2 against 76.2% at >=+2), so it can demote but never promote; no pivot beats standing the condemned pick (stand 82.22%, tip 3 78.17% even where one exists, tip 2 68.29%), so only NONE is better; and priced on 5,981 rungs at real closing odds the ROI goes -1.86% to -1.51% with the whole gain in the older window (-1.25 to -0.15) while the newer one worsens (-2.47 to -2.84). Depth does NOT help — beyond ten cards of club history the effect is flat at +2.4 to +3.3 and the sharpest separation is in the THINNEST bucket (+6.90) where the club slices cannot vote at all; the staleness explanation for that was tested and rejected, since windowing the slices is worse at every length (cumulative +2.17 against last-8 +1.85 and last-60 +1.96). CORRECTED the same day on two counts. First, that ablation table was NOT selectivity-matched — the claim row keeps 25.7% of cards and the six-search row 41.8%, and a stricter rule buys hit rate for free, so the pairing did not support the weight put on it; the six-search line is a real result on its own terms. Second, matched properly, the score IS additive: blending claim rank with score rank optimises at w=0.2-0.5 rather than 0, and inside the claim's own top 40% the score sorts the survivors monotonically across quartiles in both windows. The six searches also double-count — in a league that leans one way "Pisa" and "Pisa on unders" are the same thirty cards — and making the crossing report a residual against the club's own rate instead of the league removes the overlap, holding the signal while cutting its cross-window gap from 1.38 points to 0.09. Then the bank was DOUBLED to 62,528 graded cards (1,500 fixtures per league, ~4 seasons) to settle the bettor's tank question directly, and the effect roughly HALVED: the quartile spread inside the claim's top 40% falls from +3.57 to +2.08 and the blend's gain from +0.10 to +0.07 at keep-40%. Everything survives in sign, nothing in size — more data shrank the finding rather than confirming it, which is the honest answer to whether filling the tank helps. Priced on 8,121 final picks at real closing odds: everything -1.67%, claim top 40% -1.57% at 86.2% hit, blended top 15% -0.96% (n=245, +/-2.03, a lead not a result), and claim-top-40-best-quartile -2.44% — WORSE than the claim alone in both windows at the same hit rate, because the extra selectivity picks shorter prices than it picks winners. Selection 1 is the whole project in one line: 4.4 points of hit rate bought 0.1 points of ROI while the average quote fell 1.16 to 1.13. RE-CHECKED once more and two claims fell. The red-tier INVERSION does not exist: it came from ~420 and ~1,630 cards on the shallow bank with the sign score, and on 62,528 cards with the de-duplicated continuous score red sorts the normal way at +2.29, positive in both windows. Promotion is still wrong, but for a different reason — red's BEST score quartile grades 79.27% against orange's WORST at 81.64%, so red's ceiling sits under orange's floor, which is a claim about levels the data supports rather than about direction, which it does not. And the era instability (+2.14 older / +0.90 newer shallow, against +1.48 / +3.04 deep) was the wrong cut entirely: it is not league mix, whose shares barely move between halves, it is REGION. The effect is European — +3.57 quartile spread in Europe with both windows positive, EXACTLY ZERO in the Americas at -0.06 (and -0.41 in one half), and RoW at +4.27 on 5,929 cards swinging +5.77 to +1.75, too thin to read. So the finding is not 'a card can be scored against its own searches' but 'a card in a European league can be'. That also kills the blended top-15% selection as a lead: it is 23.8% RoW against 9.5% of the bank, two and a half times over-represented in exactly the region where the score does not work, so its -0.96% on 245 cards is a noisy sub-population landing favourably rather than a signal. Club memory swept properly — windowing ONLY the club reads, leaving league and side cumulative — is NEUTRAL, every setting from last-20 to last-730-days within 0.15 points; last-40 ships as a reasoned default because it never loses and squads really do change, not as a measured gain. That sweep also explains an earlier wrong conclusion: the previous windowing test cut the league-side slice too, a statistic built from hundreds of cards with no staleness problem, which is why it showed harm. Orange because the residual is worth a fourth, small, ONE-DIRECTIONAL input to the existing guard, applied to EUROPEAN leagues only, sized for +2 to +3.5 points — and not a five-colour system, not a reroute rule, and not a reason to enlarge the bank

column4: Can a green/orange/red risk guard, read off Athena's own card before any result is known, flag the plays that go wrong? (green = a gated DNB or tip 1 claiming >=84% on an edge under 1.0; red = tip 1 under 76%, or under 80% on an OVER; orange = the rest)
column5: It separates HITRATE reliably and ROI only in one window. Graded on 7,673 final picks settled at football-data's maximum closing price across 16 European leagues — result lanes derived exactly from 1X2, ladder rungs through a mu fitted to the 2.5 line — the whole book returns -1.70% (82.1% at 1.15). By tier: green 87.0% hit / -1.05%, orange 82.5% / -1.08%, red 75.8% / -4.30%. Dropping red lifts the book to -1.07%, so the answer to 'will red take out most of the bad ones' is yes on strike rate. But the two-window split refuses the money claim: older half red -1.17% against green -0.91% and orange -0.88% — worth nothing — while the newer half runs red -6.28%. The hitrate gap holds in BOTH halves (86.7 vs 77.2 older, 87.3 vs 74.9 newer), so what red really marks is a lower strike rate that the market sometimes prices correctly and sometimes does not. Independent support from the thin-league run the same day: green -2.47% against orange -4.40% on 836 picks. Ships as a CONFIDENCE colour on the card, not as a profitability filter — -1.07% is still a loss, and half the evidence for the lift is one time period

column4: Are thin markets softer, so the final pick can pay there even though it cannot in Europe? (the framing behind the two best live overlays — Jong PSV at 1.44 against a 1.21 consensus, and America-MG U3.5)
column5: No, and the premise is wrong on the market we actually bet. Backfilled the-odds-api across BRA-SB, CHI-PD and SAU-PL — three leagues with no football-data feed at all — for ~3,200 credits and 239 snapshots, deliberately excluding the UEFA cups as the most liquid markets on the board. On 854 graded picks: thin-league TOTALS carry 5.09% overround at the best price across real books (n=1,763) against Europe's 5.60% — slightly TIGHTER, not wider. The fat margin is on 1X2 at 8.53% (n=8,390), which is a genuinely soft market, but the ladder is where the picker spends most of its plays. A small book copies a good totals line, because totals are trivial to arbitrage, and works its margin into the result market instead. Returns follow: -2.90% +/-1.36 there against Europe's -1.70%, on a HIGHER hitrate (85.9% vs 82.1%) at a SHORTER average price (1.12 vs 1.15) — these books know which matches are safe. BRA-SB -3.38%, CHI-PD -1.41%. Dropping red makes it worse (-3.13%) because red is 18 of 854 cards. What this does NOT close: NED-D2, the reserve league that produced the 1.44-vs-1.21 gap, is carried by neither feed and stays unmeasured. Two anecdotes were framed as a strategy ahead of their evidence; what survives is only that the edge, if any, sits in markets too thin for anyone to sell data on

column4: Does the shot-blended forecast turn its better Brier into ROI? (at short prices its edge gradient ran the RIGHT way for the first time — -1.29% at 2 points of claimed edge rising to +3.35% at ten)
column5: No. The gradient was one hot window. Split by date over 1,936 fixtures carrying both a blended forecast and a market line, the entire positive result sits in the older half and the newer half is negative at EVERY threshold: at 5 points of edge +5.51% older against -7.41% newer, at 8 +12.16% against -5.49%, at 10 +18.30% against -8.51%, at 12 +22.15% against -11.11%. The newer half also gets WORSE as the edge bar rises, which is the same anti-predictive shape every other lane family showed, and the hitrate on one identical rule runs 83.7% older against 65.5% newer. What survives is only the accuracy claim, which was validated separately: the blend closes 33% of the Brier gap to the market on this same joined sample. Better forecasting and better betting remain measurably different things

column4: Are the goal-expectation ratings better built from SHOTS ON TARGET than from goals? (the store already holds hst/ast; goals are the noisy realisation and shots regress better between matches)
column5: Measured and promising, not yet in the engine. scripts/shot_ratings.py replays both models as-of in one forward pass with an identical functional form, window, shrinkage and Poisson scoring — only the statistic differs — and scores them on U1.5/U2.5/U3.5/U4.5, four lines neither model selects. Run over ALL 128,532 fixtures the store holds. Shots ALONE are not reliable — -1.09% overall, and -2.37% in the older half, which is what patchy shot recording in the thinner leagues and older seasons looks like. But a MIXTURE beats goals alone and does it in both windows independently: w=0.4 on shots gives +0.96% of Brier overall, +0.80% in the older half (which prefers w=0.3) and +1.24% in the newer (which prefers w=0.5). The optimum is a flat basin from 0.3 to 0.5, not a spike, which is what a real effect looks like rather than a fitted one. On the 8 richest leagues alone the same sweep gives +1.07% at w=0.6. For scale, the whole gap to the bookmaker's closing line is 2.3%, so this is roughly half of it. CAVEAT that governs what happens next: the baseline here is a standalone goals model scoring 0.1925, while the real engine scores 0.1876 — it is already better than the thing shots beat, so the gain cannot be assumed to transfer. The next step is the shots signal inside the real pipeline, re-measured the same way. One bug found and fixed mid-experiment: an all-time cumulative conversion rate penalised only the shots model and reversed the whole result, turning +0.35% into -3.01%

column4: Star tip 3 only when it is a DNB claiming more than 2 points above tip 1 — otherwise always star tip 1 (fell out of testing the profile chooser above)
column5: Validated and not yet shipped. The shipped chooser is measurably behind always taking tip 1: 82.09% against 83.64% on the 17,995-card walk-forward, and 82.08% against 83.49% on the project's own tables (final_pick.tsv against baselines.tsv, 57 leagues, picker worse in 36 of them). It drops to tip 3 whenever tip 1 is not playable, and tip 3's baseline sits five points below tip 1's, so it trades down by construction. The gate fixes the trade: on the 426 cards where a DNB out-claims tip 1 by more than 2 points, the DNB grades 94.13% against tip 1's 82.16%, +11.97. It holds with DNB pushes stripped out entirely (+9.58 on 355 cards), so it is not a settlement artefact, and it clears BOTH windows independently (+7.44 older, +16.59 newer; +5.79 and +13.94 with pushes removed). It also holds whether or not tip 1 is playable (+11.38 playable, +13.86 not), so it needs no playable exception. DOUBLE CHANCE must be excluded: at the same gate a DC switch LOSES 3.53 points. Whole-board effect is small because it fires on 1.42% of cards (+0.170 points over always-tip-1) — the real gain is the 1.7 points from retiring the current rule

column4: Should the chooser look the card's PROFILE up in the bank and take whichever lane has graded best on similar cards? (the bettor's proposal: filter by league plus each lane's kind and probability, then also by home and away side, and let the empirical hitrates pick)
column5: Built and replayed walk-forward over 17,995 cards — each card sees only its own league's earlier matches, never itself or anything later. It loses to simply always taking tip 1 in every configuration: 82.45% at a +/-3 claim band against always-tip-1's 83.64%, and 82.2-83.2% across bands of 2 to 8 and sample floors of 15 to 50. Restricting the neighbourhood to the two clubs made it WORSE (82.20%), as the team-persistence measurement predicts. The cause is estimator quality, not the idea: a neighbourhood hitrate re-estimates a lane's probability from 30-100 cards, where the printed claim is built from thousands, so the lookup swaps a good estimate for a noisier one and then acts on the noise. This is also why the manual filter searches feel so informative and do not convert — they re-derive a number the card already prints

column4: Does tip 2's KIND say which other lane to trust? (the bettor read it off the filter: team-over cards showed tip 1 at 91% and tip 3 at 80%, team-under cards the reverse at 72% and 92%)
column5: No. Replayed over 16,583 fixtures with tip 2's market in the dump: tip 1 is essentially INVARIANT to tip 2's kind — 82.7 on team-over cards, 83.1 on team-under, 84.7 ladder-over, 83.3 ladder-under, 84.4 with no tip 2 at all. A two-point range across four thousand-fixture buckets. The session's 91-versus-72 split was a 20-point gap between samples of 89 and 18 in a goal-heavy week. One real thing did fall out: tip 3's reliability DOES move with tip 2's kind (82.1 on team-over cards against 73.9 on ladder-over), but it never overtakes tip 1, so it changes nothing about the chooser. The proposed mechanism — a team under implying a decisive match — was a story fitted to noise

column4: Should the chooser prefer a different lane PER LEAGUE? (the bettor read it off the new filter counters: tip 1 strong in England/Italy/MLS, tip 3 in Germany, tip 2 in France, tip 3 in Norway)
column5: Measured two ways and declined. (1) The 300-match replay per league disagrees with most of it: tip 1 leads in 18 of 20 leagues, including Germany (86.0 vs 80.3) and France (79.9 vs 66.4) where the session slice said otherwise. Only BRA-SA and NOR-EL show tip 3 ahead — Norway 85.4 vs 83.9, the one country read the replay corroborates. (2) The chooser variant scored out of sample (learn each league's best lane on its older half, score on the newer): 83.61% against always-tip-1's 83.71%. Learning the preference buys nothing even when it is allowed to learn. The cause is sample size: a session slice of 18 lanes at 80% carries a standard error of 9.4 points, so a 15-point country gap is one noisy weekend. The counters are a fine lens for spotting questions and a poor one for answering them — which is why the replay exists

column4: The star restricted to tip 1 or tip 3 (the bettor's follow-up to the final-picking table)
column5: Scored offline from the upgraded dump — the instrument now stores every lane's grade per fixture, so a variant costs a query instead of a replay. Dropping tip 2 recovers most of the loss: 79.5% -> 82.1% league-average, against always-tip-1's 83.5%. The residue is one honest swap: on the 3,715 fixtures with no playable tip 1 but a printed result lane, tip 3 lands 77.9% where tip 1 lands 84.3%. On HITRATE the star should never leave tip 1. On MONEY it can — the swap pays if the result lane is priced 8%+ above the total, which the buy>= bracket already answers per card. Orange because the money side is unmeasured: no odds history exists to settle it, and the live book is the only instrument that can

column4: Final picking: is the card's starred lane better than always taking tip 1?
column5: No — measured before trusting it. The star's chooser replayed per league at n=300 (16,554 graded fixtures, bank freshly merged with the board's own results): league-average 79.5% against always-tip-1's 83.5%. Every deviation costs — tip 2 picks grade 72.6 where tip 1 would have graded 85.3 (−12.7), tip 3 picks 77.2 vs 83.1 (−5.9). The finding underneath is the valuable one: a tip 1 that MISSES the playable bar still lands 84.5%, because a thin edge means the league's baseline is already high, not that the tip is weak. The star stays (one preferred lane per card was the ask) but now yields to any playable tip 1, and is labelled read-first rather than best-bet — the buy≥ bracket decides what to buy. The About protocol's step 2 was corrected the same day it was written

column4: Is the DNB lane itself broken? (the book's 0W 4P 4L asked it)
column5: Deep-dived on the 15,048-fixture result-lane dump with the shipped tilt and gates replayed: DNB is the BEST-calibrated thing tip 3 does — DNB1 says 73.2, wins 77.4 of decisive (+4.2) on 3,833 prints; DNB2 +11.7; every claimed band underclaims, monotonically (+1.7 at says 65-70 up to +8.7 at 85-90); pushes 23%. The live session agrees (18W 10P 8L, 69% of decisive). The book's 0-for-11 is the ticket SHAPE, not the prediction: three unpriced own-reads, short odds under the printed buy-from, and a push rate double the expected 23% in an 11-ticket sample. Rule 7 already carries the fix. One flag for later: the 12 lane is tip 3's only OVERclaimer (says 75.3, lands 73.3 on 7,884 prints) — worth a look before any 12-heavy strategy leans on it

column4: A min or max stated-probability filter on the tips would lift the hitrate
column5: Banded says-vs-hit on the current dumps, last 300 per league, two half-windows: Tip 1 calibrates at every band (worst −1.4, the 70-75 band OVER-delivers +5.7/+2.5), and the team lanes behind Tip 2's cold tile calibrate too — the O1.5s claiming 55-65 hit 58 on a 59 claim in BOTH halves. Nothing overclaims consistently at either end, so a probability cut would only refuse honest low-claim lanes to flatter the tile — the GRE-SL floor mirage again. Declined; instead the tiles now print the family's average CLAIM beside its hit (tip 2: 63.3 vs claims 69.0), so a low number reads as what it promised, not as failure

column4: Tip 3 — the result lane (1X/X2/12, sharpening to DNB when one side dominates), the bettor's proposal, SHIPPED ON PROBATION
column5: Measured first on 15,048 fixtures across 52 leagues (scripts/result_lanes.py): the per-side expectations through two Poissons price the result market honestly once the home side is tilted 1.10 (raw home wins ran +3.2 hot in both halves; tilted, all six outcome gaps close within 1.4). The feared Poisson draw bias never appears — TEAM_SHRINK compresses the sides and pumps the draw by roughly what Poisson drops it. The strongest-DC band that supplies three quarters of prints grades +0.1/−0.5; every stronger band and every DNB band UNDERCLAIMS (+1.3 to +8.5) — the lane's failure mode is modesty. Prints from DC_FLOOR 0.72 with edge ≥2 over the league's as-of base rate; DNB upgrade at 0.65 of the no-draw mass. Outside every tally and the hero until live results earn it in, exactly the cup lane's probation path

column4: Team-lane side attribution fails on regime breaks — the bettor's hypothesis from the Yukun/Forest cards: recent staff and squad churn shows up as a form streak the engine mistakes for quality
column5: Measured on 8,404 replayed team-lane offers across 52 leagues (scripts/team_attrib.py): ALIGNED divergence — the last-8 scoring stub vs the long record, signed toward the rung — is monotone with overclaim: deflated +3.3, stable +1.2, mild inflation −1.7, strong (0.8+) −3.2 with both half-windows negative (−3.9/−2.5). The proposed data inputs measured differently: DEPTH of record (thin history) showed no consistent effect and shipped nothing, and league tables would have argued FOR the Yukun pick ("chasing the top"). STREAK_FROM 0.35 / STREAK_SLOPE 0.05 ships on the published number; treated region closes to +0.4/−1.0 per half; ~2.7% of offers stop printing. One-sided as always — deflated reads keep their honest underclaim. Honest limit: the debit fixes the population, not every anecdote — Yukun's own offer drew only 1.9 points because its edge came mostly from Zhejiang's base rate

column4: A push should count as a win at the ROOT, not just in the tallies — the bettor's rule: the standing offset plays U3.0 as U3.5, so the actual play wins where the printed rung pushes
column5: The board's counters, playable tallies and hero window now grade ◦ as a hit (shipped 29 Aug). The deeper change — hit_weight("push")=1.0, which would fold push totals into winning_totals and hence into the PUBLISHED probabilities and selection ties — is a real engine change: U3.0 would collapse into the U3.25/U3.5 tier, tips would reshuffle, and every baseline (retrosim table, REL bases, floors) needs re-derivation on two windows before it ships. Until then the claims exclude the push and the tally credits it, which overstates hit vs says by the push rate (~1-2 points on U3.0-heavy lanes) — known, accepted, and queued

column4: The Playable-hit column's collapse leagues — the bettor spotted IRL-PD 83.2 falling to 68.6 on 35 lanes, CRO-1L and MEX-LMX similar
column5: Confirmed and diagnosed on a 29,763-tip current-engine replay (retrosim --dump). Board-wide the playable layer is honest — says 82.3, hit 82.1, gap −0.1 on 15,813 lanes — and no playable-bar height beats +1% (raising it LOWERS hit in both halves), so the bar stands. The collapse is seven specific leagues (CRO-1L, MEX-LMX, IRL-PD, MAR-BP, COL-PA, ESP-L2, ITA-SA) whose positive-edge lanes overclaim >4 points in BOTH half-windows — pooled −6.4/−7.5 — flat across edge size, while their consensus lanes underclaim +3.4: there, disagreeing with the league consensus IS the model's error. The implied proportional debit (k≈2.0/2.3) empties their playable set anyway, so the honest ship is the CONSENSUS CAP: published probability capped at the market's league-baseline chance, edge can never exceed zero, no lane there ever badges playable. Board playable hit rises 82.1 → 82.6 (82.4→82.9 / 81.8→82.3 per half). Selection untouched, as always

column4: The buy≥ gate prices REL-debited and capped lanes from the raw engine number
column5: _undebited() reverses the cup-over and high-says debits but not REL or the consensus cap, so a debited lane's printed buy≥ sits a few percent below its honest break-even. Capped lanes all land sub-bar where nothing is bought, and REL rarely bites hard on board lanes — small, but the gate run backwards should someday reverse everything the gate applies

column4: A tip claiming far more than its league's proven base rate is bragging — the bettor's hypothesis, confirmed one-sided
column5: Measured on 32,493 replayed tips against each league's own hit rate: within ±2 points the claims are honest (gap −0.1); past +2 every extra claimed point delivers ~−1.2 back (slope −1.27/−1.04, both windows), and the wide-high band ran 5.6 hot in BOTH halves — while wide-LOW tips deliver their claims or better, so only one side is diseased. Filtering would lift playable hit just 86.4 → 86.7 (the braggarts still hit ~84); the real leak was the CLAIM, so REL_SAYS_DEBIT ships instead: 1.1 × the excess above league+2, published number only, selection raw. Every band closes to ±1.1 in both windows

column4: Proof in hindsight: the losing era was volume, not the engine's ceiling
column5: The pre-calibration weekend — 69.9% across 73 bets taken 'just going with it', ROI −10.1% — replayed through today's engine grades 84.2% taking every Tip 1 (avg buy≥ 1.30) and 83.3% at the playable bar. On the first calibrated slate the +1% bar filters 63 lanes to 42 and hits 95.0%: selection keeps the best winners. In-sample caveat attached — these weeks are the windows the constants were tuned on, so this is a ceiling estimate; the live confirmed number (84.6% on tips published before kickoff) landing in the same neighbourhood is the corroboration

column4: The weakest leagues can be lifted the way the cups were — but only under an ROI constraint
column5: Raised floors climb selection to safer rungs and lift hitrate in both windows everywhere — but the first pass measured only hitrate, and GRE-SL's 80.9 → 91.7 turned out to cost 66% → 6% of PLAYABLE volume (buy≥ 1.37 → 1.19): safe rungs nobody can buy edge on. Final rule: highest floor keeping ≥2/3 of playable volume. Six leagues ship 0.82, one 0.80, seven 0.78; GRE-SL and PER-L1 revert; MLS (worse at any floor) and ITA-SB (nothing to climb to) never shipped

column4: Above says 90% the domestic board is too sure of itself
column5: Measured on 32,493 tips across 45 leagues: below 90% the gap is −0.2 (honest); at 90%+ it is −1.2 ± 0.3, holds in both windows (−1.0 / −1.5) and is STRONGER in the played population (−1.8 / −1.4). Flat inside the band, so HIGH_SAYS_DEBIT 0.012 ships on the published number — selection stays raw

column4: Per-league gaps at n=200 are mostly noise wearing a number
column5: The worst sixteen rows, re-measured at ~780 each: ROU-L1 −11.6 → −2.8, and every one of them collapsed into a band of −2.8 to +1.7 around a pooled −1.7. One row in the whole table cleared two standard errors. The table now replays up to 800 fixtures capped at two seasons

The played-lane record historically grades 1–2 points ABOVE its stated probability, which covers most of that shortfall — but not with a margin. Systematized 28 Aug as the buy-blend (BUY_BLEND_BELOW/ABOVE): the printed buy≥ itself now reaches toward the league's playable record and prints the margin it gave up, so the widened strategy is priced on the card instead of eyeballed against it

Reads now say 'by results'; no engine impact (mu never reads standings, and the pos_signed term was measured and declined). Open question: whether any consumer ever NEEDS the official table

One knockout round, ~2 SE, rhymes with the qualifiers' standing −3.2/−3.5 gaps. Untested: whether elimination-night second legs are structurally hotter than earlier rounds. Measure before the next playoff window

column5: EV at the printed buy-from across the table runs 1.02–1.15. The extremes people worry about are HONEST — ITA-SB (77.2 hit, 1.46 odds) sits near the top at 1.127, JPN-J1 (88.6, 1.20) clears 1.063 — but the overconfident rows cannot cover their own price: MLS 1.017, ESP-L2 1.025, MEX-LMX 1.027, UEL-Q 1.033, FRA-L2 1.055. Their fix is per-league calibration or a cull, not floor tuning. ESP-L2 and MEX-LMX resolved 28 Aug by the consensus cap (no playable lanes to misprice); MLS, UEL-Q and FRA-L2 still pending

column4: TUR-SL and ESP-L2 are overconfident in their RECENT two seasons
column5: The only two rows that survive the noise-aware re-measure: TUR-SL −5.2 (n 391), ESP-L2 −4.3 (n 525) — both read fine over a longer trail (−2.6 / −2.8 at n≈740), so the miss is concentrated in the current window. Cause not yet diagnosed

column4: IRL-PD and MAR-BP price on a mu that carries no information
column5: At n≈800 IRL-PD's residual slope is −2.8 (t −3.0) and NEGATIVE IN BOTH WINDOWS — mu is anti-correlated with outcomes there; MAR-BP reads −0.8 (t −2.2). Their hitrates survive because the league mean carries them, but the stated probabilities pretend knowledge. RESOLVED 28 Aug by the consensus cap: both are in CONSENSUS_CAP_LEAGUES, so their published numbers never claim more than the league baseline and no lane there badges playable — the cull happened at the claim layer, and the tips stay on the board honestly
